severity.changeConditions: downgrade to should-fix only if the packaged build is dropped from the deliverables

confidence.rationale: Reproduced: the first build ran and died with ImportError; fixed and re-run green.

findings.title: Relative import in a PyInstaller entry script
findings.summary: PyInstaller executes its entry script as `__main__` with no package context, so `from .launcher import run` raises ImportError at startup. The build reported success.
findings.recommendation: Use an absolute import. Keep tools/check_release.py in the release path — it is the only thing that executes the packaged artifact.
findings.evidence: build 1 output: `ImportError: attempted relative import with no known parent package` / `[PYI-12352:ERROR] Failed to execute script '__main__'`

severity.changeConditions: upgrade to blocker if the page is ever reachable from another origin

confidence.rationale: Probed config.check_value against 9 host shapes incl. suffix look-alikes; gated in tools/check_settings.py with a must-accept control.

findings.title: OPS base URL was free text, and the credential travels to it
findings.summary: The consumer key and secret are sent to OPS_BASE_URL as an HTTP Basic header. A typo or a pasted hostile URL in that field exfiltrates them.
findings.recommendation: Constrain to epo.org and https, in ONE validator shared by the save and test paths. Cost: 20 lines. No legitimate use is lost — the field is documented as 'leave it alone'.
findings.evidence: check_settings.py: `a host outside epo.org refused HTTP 400`, `CONTROL: another epo.org path IS accepted HTTP 200`

severity.changeConditions: upgrade to blocker if a non-user actor can reach POST /api/settings

confidence.rationale: Gated: a value containing a newline is refused and nothing lands in the file.

findings.title: A newline in a value writes a second setting
findings.summary: The settings file is one KEY=value per line. A value carrying \n injects a setting nobody asked for — reachable from the panel's own text fields.
findings.recommendation: Reject control characters at the API boundary; validate every value before writing any.
findings.evidence: check_settings.py: `newline in a value refused HTTP 400`, `nothing was injected into the file`

severity.changeConditions: downgrade to consider if hand-editing the file is declared unsupported

confidence.rationale: Reproduced in the gate: edit the file, the panel showed the new hint while `configured` and the OPS client still came from the boot-time environment.

findings.title: The panel re-read the file but not the engine
findings.summary: Two answers to one question: the hint came from the file, `configured` and the live OPS client from os.environ as loaded at startup.
findings.recommendation: _sync_from_file() re-loads and resets the client, and reports adopted_file_change so the switch is visible rather than silent.
findings.evidence: check_settings.py: `the panel shows the hand-edited key`, `and says it adopted a change rather than doing it silently`

severity.changeConditions: downgrade to consider if endpoints ever become single-threaded

confidence.rationale: Reasoned from FastAPI's threadpool execution of sync endpoints; not reproduced (needs a save concurrent with an in-flight sheet fetch).

findings.title: Closing an OPS client that another thread is using
findings.summary: reset_ops closed the old httpx client. A drawing sheet in flight on it fails with 'Cannot send a request, as the client has been closed' — a 502 caused by an unrelated settings save.
findings.recommendation: Retire rather than close; close all retired clients in Service.close(). A session saves settings a handful of times, so the held sockets are not a leak worth that risk.
findings.evidence: FastAPI runs `def` endpoints in a threadpool; api_settings_post and api_ops_page can overlap. httpx.Client.close() is not safe against a concurrent send.

severity.changeConditions: downgrade to nit if PORT is documented as developer-only

confidence.rationale: Traced: PORT set + port occupied by a stranger returned (port, None) and let uvicorn fail with a traceback.

findings.title: A pinned PORT was not probed before use
findings.summary: The env override returned its port unexamined, so a second launch on a pinned port tried to bind an occupied socket and crashed instead of standing down.
findings.recommendation: Probe the pinned port the same way as the scanned ones; raise a sentence when it is occupied by something else.
findings.evidence: check_release.py drives exactly this path: `the second copy stood down`

severity.changeConditions: upgrade to blocker if the server ever binds ::1

confidence.rationale: Counted colons by hand against both forms: '[::1]:8000'.count(':') == 4.

findings.title: Colon-counting mis-parses a bracketed IPv6 host
findings.summary: `[::1]:8000` was judged non-local and would be refused with 421. Unreachable today (IPv4-only bind) and a silent lockout the day that changes.
findings.recommendation: Parse the bracketed form explicitly. Also dropped 0.0.0.0 from the allow list — no client sends it as a Host.
findings.evidence: LOCAL_HOSTS membership test on the un-split '[::1]:8000'

severity.changeConditions: upgrade to should-fix if a document with >40 sheets becomes common

confidence.rationale: Read the code path: big.onload calls figStrip(), which replaces innerHTML.

findings.title: The page strip is rebuilt whole on every OPS page load
findings.summary: Rebuilding re-applies the current-page class correctly but loses the strip's horizontal scroll position on long documents.
findings.recommendation: Leave it. The rebuild is how 'this sheet is now paid for' gets drawn; a diffing update costs more complexity than one lost scroll position is worth.
findings.evidence: figStrip() sets innerHTML; scrollIntoView state is not restored afterwards

severity.changeConditions: downgrade to nit — real OPS keys are 24-48 chars, so the branch is unreachable in practice

confidence.rationale: Arithmetic: a 7-character value showed 4 of its characters.

findings.title: The hint exposed over half of a short value
findings.summary: The old threshold (<=6) let a 7-character value show 4 characters.
findings.recommendation: Raise to 12 and say 'much shorter than an OPS key, possibly pasted wrong' — which is the more useful answer for a short value anyway.
findings.evidence: hint('1234567') previously returned '7 字元 · 結尾 …4567'

confidence.rationale: An load exposes no response headers to script; verified against the page, which reads /api/ops/cached-pages instead.

findings.title: A docstring claimed the page reads a header it cannot read
findings.summary: X-Page-Source is useful for curl and the network panel, not for the page.
findings.recommendation: Say what it is actually for, and name what the page really asks.
findings.evidence: The strip's source of truth is loadCachedPages() -> /api/ops/cached-pages

severity.changeConditions: upgrade to should-fix — it is a stated project rule, not a preference

confidence.rationale: Compared against CLAUDE.md's 'no silent waiting' ruling (2026-08-26) and against busyOn(), which already had an elapsed counter.

findings.title: Two new waits said what, not how long
findings.summary: The settings POST and the EPO sheet fetch each showed a static message. The project's own rule requires elapsed time so a slow source and a hung one look different.
findings.recommendation: One ticker() shared by both, plus a 60 s AbortController on the POST so a hung request cannot leave the buttons disabled forever.
findings.evidence: CLAUDE.md: 'Anything taking more than ~300 ms says what it is waiting for and how long it has been waiting.'
